goal: Find public, direction-registered as-built plans/elevations for roof extent, facade assignments, and atrium stair/bridge positions.

sources_checked.publisher: Purdue University Archives and Special Collections
sources_checked.record: Neil Armstrong Hall of Engineering records, accession 2023-097, communal accessions box 59; dates 2007; listed as unprocessed material.
sources_checked.result: Catalog confirms records exist but provides no public digitized plans, elevations, or measured drawings. The record is not an architectural geometry source.

sources_checked.publisher: Fink Roberts & Petrie, structural engineer of record
sources_checked.result: Confirms a three-story cast-in-place frame, structural-steel penthouse, basement/partial sub-basement, cantilevered roof truss, two atrium bridge levels, elevated tiered lecture room, and three concrete stairs. The public page gives no measured dimensions, plan coordinates, facade stationing, or locations for those stairs/bridges/penthouse.

sources_checked.publisher: Purdue University Office of Emergency Preparedness
sources_checked.result: Confirms four levels (lower, grade, two upper floors) and room/program names. It is not a dimensioned plan or roof record.

sources_checked.publisher: Purdue e-Archives, Purdue Buildings and Campus Scenes
sources_checked.result: A 2007 photo documents the Apollo 1 replica installation in the atrium. It visually confirms a multi-level glazed atrium and balconies, but the image has no camera pose or local-frame registration.

The public webcam archive exposes construction progress imagery, not measured architectural documentation. No roof/elevation/floor-plan controls suitable for registration were found in the accessible record.
Describes current bid-document access for contractors; no public Armstrong as-built drawing set is discoverable from the public page.

modeling_decision: No R11 geometry change. The registered 2023 orthophoto and GIS indicate a slab-to-footprint mismatch, but GIS is not an architectural roof plan and some features may be canopies. FRP verifies stairs and bridges exist but supplies no coordinates. Without registered elevations/plans, trimming slabs, moving facade openings, or placing stairs would be speculative.
remaining_evidence_needed: As-built roof plan/elevation with local dimensions or control points
Direction-registered exterior elevation or calibrated imagery identifying facade window bands and roof edge
Dimensioned atrium/level plans or a pose-registered panorama showing the three stair paths and bridge endpoints
